iterations.explanation: Eight axes separate domain capabilities, integration, workflow, communication, rule variation, privacy, reporting, and session security; no previous feedback was provided.

clusters.name: Bike Location and Proximity Strategy
clusters.description: Captures how the platform represents, stores, and queries bike positions and nearby-bike availability.

relations.rationale: Rental initiation depends on discovering an available bike within the permitted service radius.

values.label: Location Service with Proximity Queries
values.description: A location-oriented service manages bike positions and supports proximity-based searches for nearby rentals.

clusters.name: Payment Integration Abstraction
clusters.description: Captures how rental and payment capabilities are isolated behind interfaces for external payment providers.

relations.rationale: Payment processing is an external integration concern that must be invoked by rental business flows without exposing provider-specific details.

values.label: Payment Facade with Internal Delegation
values.description: A payment facade exposes a simple API and delegates provider-specific processing to internal payment services.

clusters.name: Rental Lifecycle Modeling
clusters.description: Captures how the rider’s rental lifecycle is represented, sequenced, and transitioned independently of infrastructure communication choices.

relations.rationale: Rental lifecycle execution uses location discovery and can invoke payment integration at relevant lifecycle stages.
The rental lifecycle provides the business process whose completion or milestones may trigger payment actions.

values.label: State-Machine Rental Workflow
values.description: The rental process is represented as explicit states covering navigation, QR-based unlocking, duration tracking, and return completion.

clusters.name: Workflow Communication Pattern
clusters.description: Captures whether related operational actions communicate synchronously or through decoupled asynchronous events and messages.

relations.rationale: Event-driven actions can decouple operational state changes from the rental and bike-management services that consume them.

values.label: Event-Driven Asynchronous Workflow
values.description: Bike registration emits an event, and downstream bike removal occurs through asynchronous messaging rather than direct invocation.

clusters.name: Business Rule Variation Strategy
clusters.description: Captures how variable business rules are selected and extended, especially when pricing algorithms may change independently.

values.label: Strategy-Based Rental Pricing
values.description: Rental pricing is encapsulated behind interchangeable Strategy implementations, allowing pricing algorithms to vary without changing the rental flow.

values.label: Pricing-Only Strategy Boundary
values.description: Notification timing is explicitly kept outside the pricing Strategy abstraction, limiting the pattern to pricing-rule variation.

clusters.name: Personal Data Protection Strategy
clusters.description: Captures how personal information is collected and protected to support data minimization, privacy, and regulatory obligations.

relations.rationale: Privacy requirements constrain how reports expose usage history and how authenticated sessions protect personal data.
GDPR-aligned protection requirements constrain session handling and access to personal information.

values.label: Minimized Secure Registration Data
values.description: Registration collects identity and contact data, keeps location data optional, and requires secure handling of personal information.

clusters.name: Usage Report Construction
clusters.description: Captures how structured rider-facing usage reports are assembled and produced as downloadable artifacts.

relations.rationale: Usage reports may contain personal or account-linked data, so their construction and exposure must respect privacy controls.

values.label: Builder-Based Usage Reports
values.description: A Builder assembles downloadable usage-history reports through incremental, structured report construction.

clusters.name: Authenticated Session Security
clusters.description: Captures mechanisms that limit authenticated access duration and reduce risks from unattended user sessions.

values.label: Idle Timeout and Automatic Logout
values.description: Inactive sessions expire and automatically log users out, reducing unauthorized access through abandoned sessions.

saturation_history.rationale: All relevant open codes are already subsumed by the existing taxonomy. The location-management and proximity-lookup codes fit dimension 1 (Bike Location and Proximity Strategy). The payment facade, simple payment API, and internal delegation fit dimension 2 (Payment Integration Abstraction). The rental workflow, navigation, QR unlock, duration tracking, and return completion fit dimension 3 (Rental Lifecycle Modeling). The Builder-based report assembly fits dimension 7 (Usage Report Construction). The Strategy-based pricing and the explicit exclusion of notification timing fit dimension 5 (Business Rule Variation Strategy). Personal data capture, optional location data, and secure handling of personal information fit dimension 6 (Personal Data Protection Strategy). Session timeout and automatic logout fit dimension 8 (Authenticated Session Security). Finally, the event-driven registration workflow, asynchronous messaging, and registration-triggered removal fit dimension 4 (Workflow Communication Pattern). No open code introduces a genuinely new architectural concern beyond the existing dimensions for CityBike.

All relevant open codes are already subsumed by existing dimensions in the taxonomy. Repository-based data access, bike data persistence, and usage statistics querying fit Dimension 9 (Data Access Strategy). Command pattern encapsulates rental operations fits Dimension 3 (Rental Lifecycle Modeling). Notification scheduling explicitly excluded and event delivery mechanism required for notifications are covered by Dimension 4 (Workflow Communication Pattern) and its boundary conditions. Biometric thumb-based authentication, immediate post-authentication biometric deletion, email/password authentication, secure credential transmission, secure credential storage, and TTL-based verification code/limited-time verification enforcement are all covered by Dimension 8 (Authentication and Session Security) and Dimension 6 (Personal Data Protection Strategy), where the axis of variation separates authentication mechanisms from privacy/minimization choices. Payment provider API normalization and common payment interface abstraction are already captured by Dimension 2 (Payment Integration Abstraction). No open code introduces a genuinely new architectural concern beyond these existing axes for the CityBike use case.
